title: The pencil sets the meal, the day and whether it is eaten; that alone plans or logs the plate
why: Coach Milan 18 November 19:51: Ate it shows as a blue chip; is it a button or a status? 20 November 16:05: Ate it is clicked and nothing changed. 16:08: the flow with the question and the chips is not UX; rethink the flow and the design. 16:13: yes to the rethought flow. 18:57 to 19:21: the situations; a fixed set of actions, never a button that turns into a status; no scroll on a tap, ask where it happens; a summary of the plate before What do you do with it?; draw it. 20:02 to 20:08: Now (Prepare it, Ate it) and Later (Save it); Plan it from My recipes, its own ticket DT332; the meal chip only chooses, Log it logs; Eaten on the meal line, not a tag. 20:21: horrible, literal, circling. Change where the question is asked; the meal and date already say plan, log or eaten; set it in the pencil block. 20:23: Already eaten, then we tell it will count there and the math recalculates. Yes, draw.

opportunity.from: Coach Milan's own look at the B151 board and the app, 18 and 20 November 2026.
opportunity.job: At the end of a plate, log what I ate in one tap, and later see at a glance that the meal is eaten.
opportunity.kind: Too many steps, and did not understand it: the meal is chosen in two places, and the tap on Ate it changes nothing you can see.
opportunity.why_now: Every plate ends here, so every meal logged goes through it.

problem: At the end of a plate the app asks What do you do with it? and Ate it or Plan it open a second calendar. But the meal and the day already say most of it: a coming meal is a plan, a past one was eaten. The question is asked in the wrong place, and the meal is chosen twice.
story: When I set the meal and day of my plate, I want that to be the whole decision, so that the plate is planned or counted without being asked again at the end.
now: The pencil block sets meal and day only. The end asks What do you do with it? with Save it, Plan it, Ate it; Plan it and Ate it open a second calendar.
proposed: The pencil block sets three things in one place: the day, the meal, and Is it eaten? as one row: Planned, Eating now, Already eaten. The row is pre-set from the day and time; on a coming day only Planned can be chosen, on a past day only Already eaten. Under the row one line says what it does: it counts in that meal and the day is calculated again, or it goes into the plan and nothing counts until eaten, or with no meal nothing counts. Edit mode saves by itself, so that choice alone plans or logs the plate, and later changes of the plate go there too. The top line repeats it: Dinner, the day and time, Eaten, counted. The end of the plate has no question, no Ate it and no Plan it: Prepare it while it is not eaten, and Save it to My recipes as the last step.
looked_at: Earlier drawings of this ticket, all set aside 20:21: a guess at the top; a summary with Now and Later groups; a meal question under Ate it with Log it. Time alone deciding, with a question only for the meal that is now: not chosen, a late lunch eaten now needs a way to say so. An Eaten switch on the meal's row: not chosen, one fixed row reads clearer.
decision: Coach Milan 20 November 20:23: yes, draw it. Waits for his look.

ac.title: Is it eaten? in the pencil block
ac.text: Given I open the pencil and tap Dinner, when I look under the meals, then Is it eaten? shows Planned, Eating now and Already eaten, one of them marked from the day and time

ac.title: The line says what it does
ac.text: Given Dinner today is marked Already eaten, when I read the line under the row, then it says This counts in today's Dinner. Your day is calculated again

ac.title: Already eaten logs it
ac.text: Given skyr, oats and a banana on the Plate, when I tap Already eaten for today's Dinner, then the plate counts in today's Dinner on Today, with no other button

ac.title: Changes follow
ac.text: Given the plate counts in today's Dinner, when I change the banana's amount, then Dinner on Today changes with it

ac.title: A coming day is a plan
ac.text: Given I tap Monday and Lunch, when I look at the row, then Planned is marked, the other two cannot be chosen, and the plate is in Monday's Lunch in the Plan

ac.title: A past day is eaten
ac.text: Given I tap Saturday and Dinner, when I look at the row, then Already eaten is marked and Planned cannot be chosen

ac.title: No meal, nothing counts
ac.text: Given No meal selected, when I look at the block, then there is no row and the line says Nothing counts. You are just looking

ac.title: The top line says it
ac.text: Given Dinner is set as Already eaten, when I close the pencil, then the top line says Dinner, Sunday, 15 November, 20:00, Eaten, counted

ac.title: The end of the plate
ac.text: Given a plate not eaten yet, when I reach its end, then there is Prepare it and Save it to My recipes, and no question, no Ate it and no Plan it; given it is eaten, then only Save it to My recipes

unchanged: The days, the meals, the meal's time field and No meal selected in the pencil block; the X closes it.
What is it? and the moment, under the block.
What Prepare it does, and what Save it puts into My recipes.
Today and the Plan: how an eaten and a planned meal show there.
A plate from a photo (the read and Did you eat it?) and a plate from earlier (DT314), as now.
checks: Full: this changes how every plate is planned and logged, so all walkthroughs, about 45 minutes, plus the unit tests, the build and a new walkthrough for AC1 to AC9. The walkthroughs that tap the old chips and the calendar under Ate it change with this approved board. New words, so the German sweep too.

boardTitle: B151: the pencil sets the meal, the day and whether it is eaten. That alone plans or logs the plate
details: The pictures are the real app on Sunday 15 November 2026, 18:00, from one scratch build of 0.3.170, not committed. The scratch shows the status row and its lines; the counting and planning behind it are not built, so Today (B151.2g) is shown from a record put in by hand.

The new words are English drafts: Is it eaten? Planned. Eating now. Already eaten. This counts in today's Dinner. Your day is calculated again. This goes into Monday's Lunch in your plan. Nothing counts until you eat it. Nothing counts. You are just looking. Eaten, counted. Save it to My recipes.
Open for the build: a meal that already holds something (add a dish or replace), and taking Already eaten back (it leaves the day again).
